position_A_mainstream: Linear No-Threshold (LNT): every dose increase adds proportional cancer risk; no safe dose; used by ICRP UNSCEAR BEIR; Chernobyl projections use LNT extrapolation from epidemiological data (A-bomb survivors) down to low doses
position_B_alternative_or_contested: Threshold model (or hormesis): low doses may have NO effect or even BENEFICIAL effect (adaptive response); some radiobiologists argue LNT is not validated at <100 mGy; Chernobyl follow-up studies have NOT demonstrated increased solid cancer in most populations
key_data_points: LNT-based: UNSCEAR 2008 projects 6600 excess cancer deaths; IARC projects 25,000; both extrapolate from >100 mGy doses downward. Threshold evidence: liquidators at <100 mGy show no clear solid tumor excess in most studies (JCO 2019 Ukraine cohort); French Académie de Médecine 2005 argued threshold exists
current_scientific_consensus: LNT retained for radiation protection (conservative/precautionary) by ICRP but recognized as a simplification; epidemiological validation at <100 mGy extremely difficult (signal too small vs background cancer rate); UNSCEAR 2012 LOW-DOSE report: 'uncertain'
source_A: ICRP 103 2007; BEIR VII 2006; UNSCEAR 2008; Cardis 2006 BMJ doi:10.1136/bmj.38962.484444.55
source_B: Académie de Médicine/Académie des Sciences 2005 joint report; Tubiana M 2009 Int J Radiat Biol; Muckerheide 2000
notes: Key tension: ICRP uses LNT for protection standards while acknowledging epidemiological uncertainty at low doses; affects public health decisions about resettlement of contaminated areas

position_A_mainstream: UNSCEAR 2008 projects 6600 excess cancer deaths total Europe from Chernobyl fallout (collective dose ~600,000 person-Sv); UNSCEAR explicitly warns against using collective dose with LNT for low-dose projection
position_B_alternative_or_contested: IARC (Cardis 2006 BMJ) projects 25,000-60,000 excess cancers (16,000 fatal) using same LNT but different risk coefficients and geographic scope; IARC includes more countries and uses nominal risk coefficients 5-6% per Sv
key_data_points: Difference driven by: (1) UNSCEAR uses European population-specific risk coefficients; IARC uses global average coefficients (higher); (2) UNSCEAR excludes some country populations IARC includes; (3) different definitions of 'affected'; dose range 0-50 mSv for most Europeans
current_scientific_consensus: Neither projection is 'wrong' - they use different risk models; true answer cannot be determined because: small excess cancers indistinguishable from statistical noise over Europe's 700M background cancer burden; uncertainty range overlaps
source_A: UNSCEAR 2008 Annex D para D611; UNSCEAR explicit caveat against collective dose
source_B: Cardis E et al. BMJ 2006 doi:10.1136/bmj.38962.484444.55; IARC EPIC cohort data
notes: nuclear_context_comparison_REAL.csv notes this discrepancy; the 'true' number is unknowable; UNSCEAR's caution about collective dose is scientifically sound

position_A_mainstream: Liquidators (mean ~115 mSv) show NO statistically significant increase in overall solid cancer incidence in most cohort studies (Ivanov 2012 Radiat Environ Biophys; Richardson 2015 Radiat Environ Biophys)
position_B_alternative_or_contested: Some studies suggest marginal increase in specific solid cancers (melanoma; bladder cancer); IRSN French analysis suggests broader excess; lack of data and record-keeping limitations may mask a real small signal
key_data_points: Ukrainian JCO 2019 cohort (1000+ liquidators): AAPC for solid tumors not significantly elevated; Russian cohort 53772 workers (Ivanov 2012): solid tumor SIR 1.04 (95%CI 0.97-1.11); Belarus liquidator data limited
current_scientific_consensus: No consensus solid cancer excess established below ~200 mGy in liquidators; this does NOT prove no effect - may reflect statistical power limitations; consistent with LNT prediction of a small (~0.5-1% increase) indistinguishable from background
source_A: Ivanov VK 2012 Radiat Environ Biophys PMID:22318524; ukraine_solid_tumor_incidence_REAL.csv
notes: Power calculation: 200,000 liquidators at 115 mSv average; LNT predicts ~230 excess cancers above 40,000+ background cancers in that cohort; <1% excess is epidemiologically undetectable

position_A_mainstream: Real radiation-induced thyroid cancer increase documented in children <18 at 1986 exposure; significant increase in Belarus Ukraine Russia since 1990; attributable to I-131 exposure; 5000+ cases confirmed
position_B_alternative_or_contested: Some fraction of observed thyroid cancer increase after 1990s is overdiagnosis from intensive ultrasound screening (detecting subclinical microcarcinomas that would never cause symptoms); thyroid_cancer_sir_trends_REAL.csv notes PTC overdiagnosis 2006-2019
key_data_points: UNSCEAR 2017: thyroid cancer excess in those exposed <18 in 1986 is real and confirmed; however post-2000 continuing rise in thyroid cancer is likely partly overdiagnosis (same trend seen in non-contaminated countries); NCI UkrAm ERR/Gy=1.91 incident but lower mortality risk
current_scientific_consensus: Radiation-attributable thyroid cancer in 1986 child cohort: established beyond doubt; overall thyroid cancer trend: partly radiation-induced (1990-2000) partly overdiagnosis (post-2005); mortality impact limited (>98% papillary cancer survival)
source_A: UNSCEAR 2017 thyroid white paper; thyroid_cancer_by_period_REAL.csv; nci_ukraine_thyroid_cohort_REAL.csv
source_B: thyroid_cancer_sir_trends_REAL.csv; Vaccarella S 2016 N Engl J Med on overdiagnosis
notes: The 'Chernobyl thyroid cancer' narrative is often overstated for mortality; the real excess in terms of DEATHS is ~15-20 thyroid cancer deaths confirmed to 2005 (WHO 2006)

position_A_mainstream: CVD in liquidators shows ERR/Gy=0.47 (PMID:30780859) representing real radiation-induced cardiovascular risk; supported by A-bomb survivor data (ERR/Gy=0.14-0.46); biologically plausible via endothelial damage and accelerated atherosclerosis; ICRP 118 2012 acknowledges CVD as tissue reaction
position_B_alternative_or_contested: Some researchers argue CVD excess in liquidators is psychosocial (stress poverty drinking smoking) not radiation; Chernobyl liquidators have higher rates of alcohol use smoking and poverty than comparator groups; confounding inadequately controlled in some studies
key_data_points: Ivanov 2019 (PMID:30780859): controlled for age sex in Russian cohort of 53772; dose-response statistically significant; but smoking alcohol data incomplete; Zablotska 2021 Environ Int provides additional analysis
current_scientific_consensus: ERR/Gy=0.47 consistent across multiple independent liquidator cohorts AND A-bomb survivors; unlikely to be entirely psychosocial confounding; ICRP 118 recognizes circulatory disease as tissue reaction requiring dose limits revision; medical consensus shifting toward accepting radiation-CVD link
source_B: Stewart 2002 challenge; Hoffmann 2012 Am J Cardiol skeptical analysis

position_A_mainstream: INSAG-7 consensus: prompt criticality from positive void coefficient + graphite tip effect when AZ-5 pressed; positive scram reactivity +7-10β caused explosion
position_B_alternative_or_contested: Rukhadze A et al. (nucl-ex/0304024 arXiv 2003): propose explosion was not prompt criticality of fuel but prompt criticality of supercritical steam-water mixture; nuclear-steam explosion rather than purely nuclear excursion; different first vs second explosion sequence
key_data_points: INSAG-7 reconstruction: power excursion 1:23:40-01:23:44 = 4 seconds; neutron flux increase of 100-1000x; steam explosion from water flashing; graphite ejection; consistent with gamma dosimetry of contaminated graphite blocks found outside; RBMK physics supports void coefficient model
current_scientific_consensus: Rukhadze preprint (not peer reviewed); contradicts multiple independent analyses; INSAG-7 revised (1992) addressed alternative theories; mainstream consensus: prompt nuclear criticality remains the established cause; Rukhadze authors are credentialed physicists but argument not accepted by nuclear engineering community
source_A: INSAG-7 Section 4; OECD-NEA Ch.I; reactor_physics_REAL.csv; Sich 1994 Science
source_B: Rukhadze A et al. arXiv nucl-ex/0304024 2003 (preprint)
notes: See session notes on ARXIV.md; this is the 'contested physics' reference in user's file; not peer-reviewed; acknowledged alternative but not mainstream

position_A_mainstream: WHO/IAEA Chernobyl Forum 2005: ~60 direct deaths (ARS + accident); 4000 potential future deaths among most exposed groups (high-dose populations); total eventual premature deaths from radiation = thousands not hundreds of thousands
position_B_alternative_or_contested: Greenpeace 2006 report: 270,000 cancers attributable; 93,000 fatal cancers; includes all Europeans at low dose; based on LNT collective dose; Yablokov 2009 book 'Chernobyl: Consequences': up to 985,000 deaths claimed
key_data_points: WHO/IAEA uses LNT but limits to high-dose populations; Greenpeace/Yablokov apply LNT to collective dose of ~600,000 person-Sv for all of Europe; UNSCEAR 6,600; IARC 25,000; Yablokov 985,000 based on non-peer-reviewed analysis of Soviet records claiming wide range of non-cancer deaths
current_scientific_consensus: Scientific consensus: WHO/UNSCEAR/IARC range of hundreds to tens of thousands; Yablokov methodology has fundamental statistical and attribution errors (criticized by mainstream epidemiologists including those sympathetic to larger estimates); the truth lies in the UNSCEAR-IARC range
source_A: WHO Chernobyl Legacy 2005; UNSCEAR 2008; birth_defects_general_health_REAL.csv; nuclear_context_comparison_REAL.csv
source_B: Yablokov AV 2009 Ann NY Acad Sci; Greenpeace 2006
notes: Yablokov critique: Fairlie I and Sumner D (co-authors of TORCH 2006 report) disagree with Yablokov's methods even while arguing for higher estimates than UNSCEAR; mainstream epidemiologists like E. Cardis distinguish legitimate uncertainty from Yablokov overcount

position_A_mainstream: Deryabina 2015 Science Advances: wolf density 7-19x higher in CEZ exclusion zone vs reference areas; mammal population studies show NO negative population-level correlation with radiation; abandonment of human activity more beneficial than harmful radiation effects
position_B_alternative_or_contested: Moller AP and Mousseau TA multiple papers (2007-2015): reduced bird and insect abundance in high-dose areas; oxidative stress; tumor frequencies; argue radiation IS causing measurable biological harm at doses >1-100 mGy/day in most contaminated areas
key_data_points: Deryabina wolf density + camera trap mammal studies (positive); Moller/Mousseau barn swallow population declines (negative); two research groups with opposing interpretations of same ecosystem
current_scientific_consensus: Scientific community divided; Beresford 2022 PLOS ONE (meta-analysis) finds: for most wildlife populations in CEZ, exclusion from human activity is net positive even with radiation; Moller/Mousseau results disputed on methodological grounds by multiple independent teams
source_B: Moller AP Mousseau TA 2007 Proc R Soc B PMID:17311787; multiple Moller/Mousseau papers
notes: cez_wildlife_contamination_REAL.csv and cez_wildlife_population_census_REAL.csv document this debate

position_A_mainstream: UNSCEAR 2001 2008: NO statistically significant increase in congenital malformations chromosomal abnormalities or heritable mutations detected in children born to Chernobyl liquidators or contaminated area residents
position_B_alternative_or_contested: Some local Ukrainian and Belarusian health reports cite elevated birth defects in contaminated areas; non-peer-reviewed regional health statistics; psychosocial stress and poverty may affect fetal development independently of radiation
key_data_points: UNSCEAR analysis of >50 studies: combined population for detectable effect requires ~300,000 births studied with adequate controls; few studies adequate; parental doses (mean ~115 mSv) are below levels expected to produce heritable effects detectable above background based on mouse genetics
current_scientific_consensus: Consensus: no confirmed radiation-induced heritable effect; theoretical risk exists per LNT but far below statistical detection; UNSCEAR notes economic and social disruption effects on maternal health may explain some regional variations in birth outcomes unrelated to radiation
source_B: Shidlovskyi I et al.; various regional health ministry reports Belarus Ukraine
notes: Radiation geneticists note: estimated doubling dose for heritable effects ~1 Gy; average liquidator dose 0.1 Gy; expected ~10% increase in heritable mutations; far below detection given spontaneous mutation rate background

position_A_mainstream: Soviet authorities initially suppressed radiation monitoring data; evacuated Pripyat 36 hours post-accident; KGB archives show falsified dosimetry (pocket dosimeters capped at 1 Gy assigned 25 cGy to many workers); 1982 Unit 1 partial meltdown suppressed for 30 years (declassified 2016)
position_B_alternative_or_contested: Soviet press reported accident quickly by Soviet standards (April 28 brief news announcement); Gorbachev's glasnost enabled eventual disclosure; argument that secrecy was standard Cold War practice not unique to Chernobyl; Soviet nuclear workers DID receive some protection
key_data_points: Forsmark April 28 monitoring triggered international revelation; Legasov testimony 1987 IAEA Vienna was more comprehensive than previous Soviet reports; Wilson Center declassification 2016 confirmed 1982 Unit 1 incident; retrospective dosimetry reconstructs original doses
current_scientific_consensus: Historical consensus: significant information suppression occurred; delayed evacuation of Pripyat increased thyroid doses to children (26% pre-schoolers >5 Gy thyroid); KI tablets not distributed (vs Poland distributed to 18M people); data suppression is a documented fact
source_B: Wilson Center Digital Archive 2016; Legasov VP diaries 1987; INSAG-1 1986 vs INSAG-7 1992 evolution
notes: INSAG-7 (1992) significantly revised INSAG-1 (1986): INSAG-7 acknowledged design flaws; INSAG-1 had blamed operators; this revision itself reflects how information was managed initially
